draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Nelliyampathy! You're up in Kaikatty, the first town of the Nelliampathi hills, and the only way up is the 26 km road from Nemmara. It winds up 17 km of hairpin turns from Pothundi Dam, straight into tea country.
draft.hungryLine: My notes don't name any eateries up in the hills, so this is tea country first. Try a cup from the estates around you.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Nelliampathi is about a 19 min walk from here. Look out for the big tea gardens at Manalaroo and Chandramala estates on the way.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a quiet spot above the tea gardens and enjoy the cool climate the planters came up here for.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The Kaikatty Industrial Cooperative Tea Factory, set up in 1976, has been working to cut its carbon footprint.

legends.title: Gardens the British left
legends.body: Locals will tell you every tea and coffee plantation up here was started by the British for the cool climate. Later they were sold to the people of the region.

legends.title: Water for the rice fields
legends.body: At the 9th km of the road up sits Pothundi Dam, a small irrigation dam at the foot of the hills. It feeds the rice fields in the plains around it, and the forest begins right after.

tips.title: Come up from Nemmara.
tips.body: It's the only route, 26 km with many hairpin turns, so take it slow.

tips.title: Bring a layer.
tips.body: The climate up here is cool, which is exactly why the planters chose it.

story.title: Planting the hills
story.body: The British started all the tea and coffee plantations here, choosing the hills for their cool climate.

story.title: In local hands
story.body: The plantations were later sold to the natives. A.V. Thomas and Company now runs a large tea garden at Manalaroo Estate, and Veekay Tea Company is at Chandramala Estate.

story.title: A cooperative factory
story.body: The Kaikatty Industrial Cooperative Tea Factory opened in 1976 to process the area's tea. It has since worked to reduce its carbon footprint.

story.title: A hill station
story.body: Nelliyampathy is now a hill station 60 km from Palakkad, with a tea based economy. Tell me how many hairpins you counted on the way up.
